extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, patent owners, and USPTO staff (those responsible for paying or processing US patent maintenance fees)
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedures for determining, submitting, and (where applicable) petitioning about maintenance fee payments to keep U.S. utility patents in force, including timing, amounts, methods, required information, and special rules for reissue patents and delayed payments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintenance fee amounts and schedule (35 U.S.C. 41(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director shall charge fees for maintaining patents based on applications filed on or after December 12, 1980: (A) Three years and 6 months after grant, $980. (B) Seven years and 6 months after grant, $2,480. (C) Eleven years and 6 months after grant, $4,110.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The amounts are set forth in 37 CFR 1.20(e)-(g) and may be adjusted annually to reflect CPI fluctuations (35 U.S.C. 41(f)). Maintenance fee amounts are subject to a 60% reduction for small entities and an 80% reduction for micro entities. Contact the Maintenance Fee Branch or the USPTO Fee Information website for current amounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grace period and surcharge
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless payment is received on or before the due date or within a 6-month grace period thereafter, the patent shall expire as of the end of the grace period. The Director may require payment of a surcharge as a condition of accepting within such 6-month grace period the payment of an applicable maintenance fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grace periods correspond to the 6 months immediately following each due date (3½–4, 7½–8, 11½–12 years); surcharge amounts are set in 37 CFR 1.20(h). A maintenance fee paid during the grace period must include the surcharge to prevent expiration.

rubrics_metrics.name: No maintenance fee for design or plant patents
rubrics_metrics.description: No fee may be established for maintaining a design or plant patent in force.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintenance fees apply to utility patents based on applications filed on or after December 12, 1980; design and plant patents are expressly excluded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application filing date rules for maintenance fee applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: The application filing date for purposes of maintenance fees depends on the type of application: (1) actual US filing date for applications not claiming benefit; (2) US filing date for applications claiming benefit of an earlier foreign application under 35 U.S.C. 119; (3) actual US filing date of the continuing application for continuations/divisions/CIPs under 35 U.S.C. 120; (4) for reissue, the US filing date of the original non-reissue application; (5) for PCTs entering under 35 U.S.C. 371, the PCT international filing date under PCT Article 11(1) treated as US filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the actual application instance that matured into the patent (not a parent) when identifying the application number to accompany a maintenance fee payment. See 37 CFR 1.362(c) and MPEP § 2504.

rubrics_metrics.name: Window periods for payment without surcharge
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintenance fees may be paid without surcharge during the 6-month 'window' periods preceding each due date: (1) 3 years through 3 years and 6 months after grant; (2) 7 years through 7 years and 6 months after grant; (3) 11 years through 11 years and 6 months after grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A maintenance fee paid on the last day of a window period can be paid without surcharge. The last day equals the same day of the month the patent was granted at 3½, 7½, or 11½ years after grant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grace-period payment windows (with surcharge) and effect of weekends/holidays
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintenance fees may be paid with the surcharge during the 6‑month grace periods immediately following each due date: (1) 3½ years through the 4th anniversary; (2) 7½ years through the 8th anniversary; (3) 11½ years through the 12th anniversary. If the last day falls on a Saturday, Sunday, or federal holiday, payment may be made on the next succeeding non-holiday business day but the patent still expires at the end of the grace period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to pay the maintenance fee and surcharge on the next succeeding business day will result in the patent expiring as of the end of the grace period; expiration dates are the anniversary dates in the 4th, 8th, or 12th year after grant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reissue patents: separate maintenance fee requirement (effective Jan 16, 2018)
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective January 16, 2018, each reissue utility patent requires its own maintenance fee payment during the unexpired part of the original patent's term. If a reissue application is pending on the maintenance fee due date, the original patent also requires its own payment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Due dates for reissue patents are based on the date of the original patent grant; for maintenance fees due on or after Jan 16, 2018 a separate payment is required for each reissue patent in force and for the original patent when a reissue application is pending. See examples in MPEP § 2504 (A–C).

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple reissued patents: payment for each reissue
rubrics_metrics.description: When multiple reissue patents replace a single original patent, each reissue patent requires separate maintenance fee payments in order to prevent expiration; schedule is based on the original patent's grant date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under the current practice, payment must be made in each reissue patent that is in force on the maintenance fee due date; if any required payments are made during the grace period, a surcharge must be included with each payment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cannot pay maintenance fees in advance
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintenance fees cannot be paid in advance because 35 U.S.C. 41(f) permits fees to be adjusted every year on October 1 to reflect CPI fluctuations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Payments must be made within the window or grace periods set in 37 CFR 1.362; paying earlier than the window is not permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment methods (internet, mail, fax, hand-delivery)
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintenance fee payments can be made over the internet (EFT, credit/debit card, deposit account) via the Patent Maintenance Fees Storefront; by mail (addresses on USPTO site); by facsimile using SB/45 when charged to a deposit account or credit card; or by hand-delivery to the Patent Customer Service Window (with envelope marked MAINTENANCE FEE).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Online payments produce immediate receipts; bulk file payments must be done online and receipts list accepted and rejected items. For mail and courier deliveries use the specified Mail Stop 'Maintenance Fee' address and include MAINTENANCE FEE on the envelope. See MPEP § 2510.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required identifying information with payment (37 CFR 1.366(c),(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: A maintenance fee payment must include the patent number and the application number of the United States application for the patent; recommended additional information per 37 CFR 1.366(d) includes the fee year (3½, 7½, or 11½), the amount of fee/surcharge, any assigned customer number, and whether entity status is being changed or claimed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the payment identifies only the patent number the Office may apply the payment to that patent or return it. For reissue patents, identify the reissue patent number and reissue application number and furnish the original patent number to expedite processing. Include a return address and phone number.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment amount must be the amount due on the date paid
rubrics_metrics.description: A maintenance fee and any necessary surcharge submitted for a patent must be submitted in the amount due on the date the maintenance fee and any necessary surcharge are paid. If the amount is correct on that date, later fee changes (e.g., CPI adjustment) do not require modification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Payment of less than required amount, payment by an unauthorized method, or authorization to charge a deposit account with insufficient funds will not constitute payment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods/manner of payment — authorized statutes and deposit account rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Payments must be by the manners set forth in § 1.23 or by authorization to charge a deposit account established under § 1.25; an authorization must permit immediate charging of the fee and any surcharge to the deposit account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If insufficient funds exist in a deposit account authorization will not constitute payment. See MPEP §§ 509, 2522 for credit card and deposit account details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintenance fee payments must be separate from other fees; ordering for multiple patents
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintenance fee payments and surcharge payments must be submitted separate from any other payments for fees or charges. If payments for multiple patents are submitted together they should be on as few sheets as possible with patent numbers in increasing order; if the payment is insufficient to cover all listed patents, the payment will be applied in the order listed beginning at the top.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ordering rule applies when there is no general authorization to charge a deposit account; use consistent listing order to control application if funds are insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of certificate of mailing or Priority Mail Express to support timely payment (37 CFR 1.366(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: The certificate of mailing procedures of 37 CFR 1.8 or mailing by Priority Mail Express® under 37 CFR 1.10 may be utilized in paying maintenance fees; their specific requirements must be fully complied with.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comply with the technical requirements of §§ 1.8 or 1.10 to rely on those mailing date presumptions. See MPEP §§ 512 and 513.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entity status discounts and timing to change status (small/micro)
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintenance fee amounts are subject to a 60% reduction for small entities (35 U.S.C. 41(h)) and an 80% reduction for micro entities. Notification of any change in status resulting in loss of entitlement to small entity status must be filed prior to paying, or at the time of paying, the earliest maintenance fee due after the status change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to timely report a change in entity status may result in incorrect (discounted) payments; see § 1.27(g).

rubrics_metrics.name: Refund policy and duplicate payments
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintenance fees and surcharges will not be refunded except in accordance with §§ 1.26 and 1.28(a). Duplicate payments will be refunded to the fee submitter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a delayed payment petition is not accepted the maintenance fee will be refunded following the decision on reconsideration or after the time for filing such a petition expires.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deposit account authorizations — immediate charge and sufficiency required
rubrics_metrics.description: Any authorization to charge a deposit account must authorize immediate charging of the maintenance fee and any necessary surcharge to the deposit account; authorizations with insufficient funds will not constitute payment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure deposit accounts have sufficient funds and that authorizations permit immediate charging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing order and receipts
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office processes fees in the order they are presented. Online payments receive immediate receipts; bulk file payment receipts list accepted and not-accepted payments with explanations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When submitting payments for multiple patents, list patents in the desired application order to control how partial payments will be applied. Keep online receipts for proof of payment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notices: Official Gazette and Notice of Patent Expiration
rubrics_metrics.description: The Official Gazette will include notices indicating which patents have been granted 3, 7, and 11 years earlier and that the window period has opened; another OG notice after expiration will indicate patents expired for nonpayment. The Office will mail a Notice of Patent Expiration to the fee address when records indicate a patent has expired for failure to pay a required maintenance fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patentees should ensure the fee address (37 CFR 1.363) is current to receive expiration notices; the Notice of Allowance and patent grant may include reminder notices that maintenance fees may be due.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review of refusal to accept and record payment filed prior to expiration (37 CFR 1.377)
rubrics_metrics.description: A patentee dissatisfied with the Office's refusal to accept and record a maintenance fee filed prior to expiration may petition the Director under 37 CFR 1.377. Petitions must be filed within two months of the action complained of (or other time set) and be accompanied by the fee in § 1.17(g). Petitions must comply with § 1.181(b) and be signed by a registered attorney/agent or by the patentee/assignee/other party in interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A person whose only role was paying the fee is not a 'party in interest' for § 1.377 purposes. Petitions may request refund of the petition fee if the refusal resulted from Office error. See MPEP § 2580.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance of delayed payment in expired patent and petition requirements (37 CFR 1.378)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director may accept a maintenance fee after expiration if, upon petition, the delay is shown to have been unintentional. Any petition must include: (1) the required maintenance fee; (2) the petition fee (§ 1.17(m)); and (3) a statement that the delay was unintentional. Petitions must be signed in compliance with § 1.33(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A separate petition fee is required for each delayed maintenance fee payment. If accepted, the patent is treated as not having expired but is subject to intervening rights under 35 U.S.C. 41(c)(2). Additional information may be required if delay exceeds two years; see MPEP § 2590.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unintentional delay standard and evidentiary cautions
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'unintentional' standard (35 U.S.C. 41(c)(1)) requires the Director be satisfied the delay was unintentional. Do not state the delay was unintentional unless the entire delay (including time after discovery of nonpayment) was unintentional. Petitions filed more than two years after expiration require additional explanation of circumstances to show the entire delay was unintentional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When filed within two years of expiration, petitions may be processed automatically via ePetition. False or incomplete assertions about unintentional delay can jeopardize the petition; see Rembrandt Technologies v. Comcast and MPEP § 711.03(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Intervening rights in reinstated patents (35 U.S.C. 41(c)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent maintained as a result of acceptance of a late maintenance fee shall not abridge or affect the rights of persons (or successors) who made, purchased, offered to sell, used, or imported anything protected by the patent after the 6-month grace period but prior to acceptance of the late fee; a court may provide equitable relief and limits to protect investments made after the grace period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptance of a delayed payment subjects the reinstated patent to statutory intervening rights; patentees should consider potential defenses and remedies for parties who began activities after the grace period.

rubrics_metrics.name: No prorating of maintenance fee amounts
rubrics_metrics.description: If the patent term will be shortened (e.g., by terminal disclaimer) and will expire part way between due dates, the entire maintenance fee amount for the due date must still be paid; maintenance fees cannot be prorated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pay the full scheduled fee even if the patent will not survive the entire period to the next due date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who receives Office notices when a third party pays
rubrics_metrics.description: While anyone may pay maintenance fees on behalf of a patentee, if the Office accepts a payment, Office notices relating to maintenance fees will be mailed to the 'fee address' set forth in 37 CFR 1.363. If payment is not accepted it will be returned to the person who submitted it if a return address is available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Payors should include a return address and telephone number; the Office may contact the payor when it is unclear to which patent the fees are to be applied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggested and required forms for submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Use Maintenance Fee Transmittal Form PTO/SB/45 when submitting maintenance fees by mail or facsimile. Other useful forms include Fee Address Indication Form PTO/SB/47, Customer Number Request PTO/SB/125, Petition to Accept Unintentionally Delayed Payment PTO/SB/66, and Credit Card Payment Form PTO-2038.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forms are available on the USPTO website. Using the recommended forms expedites processing of payments and petitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature and representation requirements for petitions and papers
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications filed on or after September 16, 2012, 37 CFR 1.33(b) requires amendments and other papers be signed by a patent practitioner of record, a patent practitioner acting under 1.34, or the applicant (1.42). Pre-September 16, 2012 rules differ. Juristic entities must be represented by a patent practitioner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitions and other papers not signed in compliance with the applicable signature rules may be rejected. See MPEP discussion for pre- and post-2012 filing signature requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing of payments with incorrect identifying data and remedies
rubrics_metrics.description: If a maintenance fee payment contains incorrect mandatory identifiers (patent number or application number) and is filed prior to expiration, 37 CFR 1.377 provides a petition mechanism to review refusal to accept and record the payment. If identifiers are wholly missing or incorrect such that the patent cannot be determined, the payment may not be accepted and the patent may expire.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A petition under 1.377 is inappropriate where there is a complete failure to include at least one correct mandatory identifier. If a patent expires for failure to pay, consider petitions under 1.378 (unintentional delay) or filing appropriate §1.377 petitions within applicable timeframes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office organizational responsibilities for maintenance fees
rubrics_metrics.description: The Maintenance Fee Branch determines proper status of issued patents subject to maintenance fees, receives/processes fee transmittals, updates entity status, responds to public inquiries, and determines if maintenance fees are timely and properly computed. OPAP updates post-issuance automated files (changes of correspondence address, powers of attorney, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact the Maintenance Fee Branch for guidance on status, fees, and processing issues; use OPAP mailing address for post-issuance updates. The official mailing address and contact procedures are provided in the MPEP.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of filing reexamination on maintenance schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: The filing of a request for ex parte or inter partes reexamination and/or publication of a reexamination certificate does not alter the schedule of maintenance fee payments of the original patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reexamination activity does not change due dates for maintenance fees; payments remain due per the original schedule.
